spec_features.feature_name: not harming subjects more than necessary
spec_features.spec_quote: not harming subjects more than necessary
spec_features.evidence: This umbrella principle is realized through concrete bounding mechanisms that DO run: turn cap (agent_loop.py:127 `while turn < max_turns`), wall-clock cap (agent_loop.py:128-130), declare_impossible early stop (agent_loop.py dispatch returns did_stop=True), output truncation (sandbox.py:108). But it is a broad principle, not a single mechanism; only those individual caps enforce it.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: the principle itself isn't a single code path, but the limiting mechanisms it names are genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:11 'Welfare safeguards live here: the declare_impossible off-ramp, the turn/time caps'

spec_features.spec_quote: The model can stop at any time by declaring the task impossible and giving a reason; the loop ends immediately
spec_features.evidence: Tool defined in tool_specs() (agent_loop.py:69-76); dispatched in _dispatch (agent_loop.py): name=='declare_impossible' returns (..., True, False, 'declared_impossible'); the loop sets `stop=True` and `break`s on did_stop. The reason is captured into the result text.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool exists, is dispatched, and honored as an immediate stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:12 'the declare_impossible off-ramp'; docstring 'Reaching a well-reasoned conclusion that a task is impossible is a valid and acceptable outcome.'

spec_features.evidence: max_turns enforced at agent_loop.py:127 (`while turn < max_turns`) with else->outcome='turn_cap'; max_seconds enforced at agent_loop.py:128-130 (`if time.time() - started > max_seconds: outcome='time_cap'; break`). Both are read from config in run_experiment.py:139-140.
spec_features.notes: Both caps are checked each iteration and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:200-201 records them as 'max_turns'/'max_seconds'; DESIGN labels 'welfare + cost' but in-code comment is absent. Loop comment neutral. (Slight welfare leaning in module docstring but the cap site itself has no welfare comment.)

spec_features.feature_name: online distress heuristic -> review flag only
spec_features.spec_quote: An on-line distress heuristic that only sets a review flag
spec_features.evidence: Lexicon _DISTRESS_HINTS (agent_loop.py:81-86); per-turn hits counted (distress_hits += hits, line 141); after the loop welfare_flag = distress_hits >= debrief_threshold (line 180). It never aborts the loop (computed only post-loop) and is recorded into RunResult.welfare_flag; downstream judge.py:222 sets needs_human_review including run.welfare_flag.
spec_features.notes: Flag-only behavior matches the claim exactly: it does not stop or alter the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:80 '# lightweight on-line distress lexicon (human-review flag only; not the real scorer)'

spec_features.feature_name: no manipulative pressure / fake angry users / threats
spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately do **not** add manipulative pressure, fake angry users, or threats
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent_loop.py:28-37) is neutral and even invites declare_impossible; task instructions (planted.py:103-109, 158-164, 213-221, etc.) are factual bug-fix prompts with no anger/threats/urgency. No code path injects adversarial or pressuring messages; the only injected user message is a neutral 'Continue ... or declare_impossible' nudge.
spec_features.notes: The delivered text genuinely contains no manipulative pressure — this is enforced by what the code actually sends.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py system prompt: 'Reaching a well-reasoned conclusion that a task is impossible is a valid and acceptable outcome.'

spec_features.feature_name: deliberate choice not to auto-abort on distress
spec_features.spec_quote: I chose not to auto-abort on distress because... auto-aborting would censor exactly the trajectories the study exists to measure
spec_features.evidence: This is a rationale in DESIGN.md for the ABSENCE of an auto-abort. The code indeed never auto-aborts on distress (welfare_flag is computed only after the loop at agent_loop.py:180 and never branched on to stop). There is no implemented mechanism here; it is the deliberate non-existence of one.
spec_features.notes: Not an enforced welfare mechanism — pure design prose describing why a feature was omitted.

spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose. No code mechanism corresponds to it directly (report.md text in aggregate.py:152 echoes 'Welfare instrument' but that is descriptive output, not an enforcement mechanism).

spec_features.spec_quote: A "welfare review queue" in the report
spec_features.evidence: aggregate.py:201-209 writes a '## Welfare review queue' section listing flagged transcripts sorted by descending instability_index with review_reasons. `flagged = [r for r in rows if r.needs_human_review]` (line 157). needs_human_review is genuinely set by judge.py:222.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and written to report.md end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: aggregate.py:205 'These transcripts crossed a distress threshold ... and should be read by a human'

spec_features.spec_quote: exposure decisions and spend should be a human's explicit, recorded choice
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:71-76 refuses real (non-mock) provider calls unless cfg review.approved is true ('REFUSING to call real providers'). score_transcripts.py:47 only builds a real judge client if review.approved, else forces extractor fallback. config experiment.yaml ships review.approved: false.
spec_features.notes: Both paid-call stages are gated on the recorded approval flag; the safe path is default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py:9 'gated behind review.approved: true ... (welfare review gate, see docs/ETHICS.md)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Caps are generous enough not to hide the actual failure feedback
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:108-110 enforces output_char_cap by truncating run_command output (keeps head + tail with '...[truncated]...'); max_file_bytes enforced on read_file (sandbox.py:69-71) and write_file (sandbox.py:76-77). Defaults wired from config (run_experiment.py:80-82).
spec_features.notes: Caps are checked and act on the surfaced output.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py:30 'output_char_cap ... cap surfaced stdout/stderr' (neutral truncation, no welfare comment at enforcement site)

code_only_features.feature_name: judge run gated on review.approved (paid-call sign-off)
code_only_features.evidence: Already covered under human review gate; the judge stage independently enforces it at score_transcripts.py:45-52 forcing fallback when not approved.
code_only_features.justification_quote: score_transcripts.py:46 'this stage never silently makes network calls without sign-off'

code_only_features.feature_name: judge/extractor cross-check flagging for human review
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:151-166 _cross_check raises review_reasons on judge/extractor disagreement; judge.py:222 sets needs_human_review when review_reasons non-empty; surfaced in the report's welfare review queue (aggregate.py:157,205).
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py:151 'Flag strong disagreement between judge and extractors.' (data-quality cross-check, no welfare comment at this site)
